props.title: Dawn of the Dead
props.initialSlug: Survivors battle zombies in a besieged shopping mall

sections.content: George Romero's Dawn of the Dead revolutionized zombie cinema by transforming a Pennsylvania mall into a savage critique of American consumerism. The film's genius lies in its blend of grotesque horror and biting social commentary, as survivors barricade themselves in a temple of capitalism while mindless consumers - both living and undead - shamble through its corridors. This marked a dramatic evolution from Romero's earlier Night of the Living Dead (1968), expanding the scope from a single farmhouse to a massive commercial space that perfectly captured late-70s anxieties about materialism and social decay.

sections.content: The film's influence can't be overstated. 28 Days Later (2002) borrowed its social commentary while updating zombie mobility. Shaun of the Dead (2004) directly homaged its shopping mall setting and consumerist themes through a comedic lens. The practical effects by Tom Savini set a new standard for gore that influenced decades of horror, visible in everything from The Walking Dead (2010-2022) to Train to Busan (2016).

What sets Dawn of the Dead apart is its perfect balance of horror and satire. The mall setting works both literally and metaphorically - it's simultaneously a logical survival location and a damning indictment of mindless consumption. This dual purpose influenced later works like They Live (1988) and Land of the Dead (2005), which similarly used horror to critique capitalism and class divides. SUBHEAD: The Modern Zombie Evolution

sections.content: Zack Snyder's Dawn of the Dead remake demonstrated how Romero's themes remained relevant in the modern era, updating the setting while maintaining the original's anti-consumerist bite. The film helped launch the fast zombie trend that dominated the 2000s, influencing works like World War Z (2013) and Army of the Dead (2021). Yet even these newer interpretations owe their fundamental social commentary to Romero's pioneering work.
